newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand posts monthly budget surplus in April.
newsitem.headline: Thailand posts monthly budget surplus in April.

text.p: Thailand posted a 7.59 billion baht ($292 million) monthly cash surplus in its operating budget in April, up from 0.6 billion in March but against a 14.9 billion baht surplus a year ago, the finance ministry said on Tuesday.

The ministry said, however, that the government operating budget posted a 36.8 billion baht deficit during the first seven months of the 1996/1997 (October/September) fiscal year against a 49.0 billion baht surplus a year ago.

Thailand's sharply slowing economy has reduced government tax revenue. The Bank of Thailand projected on Monday that the government's operating budget will end the current fiscal year with a 23.1 billion baht deficit against a 104.3 billion baht surplus during 1995/1996.
The expected deficit this year would be Thailand's first in 10 years, in line with its sluggish economy. The economy is expected to expand 5.9 percent this year, its slowest pace since 1986.
